title: Transition behavior under tape embedding
statement: Let $m,k$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a set of states, let $	ext{Symbol}$ be an alphabet, and let $M$ be a Turing machine with $m$ work tapes. Given an injection from the $m$ work-tape indices into the $k$ work-tape indices, a state $q\in S$, an optional input symbol, and a choice of optional symbol for each of the $k$ work tapes, the transition of the machine obtained by embedding $M$ into $k$ work tapes has the same input-head movement, output, and successor state as the transition of $M$ on the symbols at the embedded indices. On each embedded index it has the corresponding work-tape action of $M$, and on every index outside the image it prescribes no write and zero movement.
hypotheses_covered: A state set $S$ and symbol alphabet
An injection from $m$ tape indices to $k$ tape indices
An optional symbol assigned to each of the $k$ work tapes
